# File Provenance | Microsoft 365 + Endpoint
**Investigate a single file path:** observed identity activity, audit chronology, explicit file movements, and a relationship graph.

Select a **Subscription**, **Log Analytics workspace**, enter an **exact full path/URL**, and set a **Lookback**. All times are UTC. **No evidence does not mean no activity.**

parameters.name: Workspace
parameters.label: Log Analytics workspace
parameters.query: resources | where type =~ "microsoft.operationalinsights/workspaces" | order by name asc | project id, name, group=resourceGroup

parameters.name: FilePath
parameters.label: Exact file path or SharePoint URL
parameters.description: Provide at least a folder and filename; full URL or C:\...\file.ext. No wildcard.

content.json: > **Investigation scope:** Read-only. Uses `OfficeActivity` (SharePoint/OneDrive audit) and `DeviceFileEvents` (Sentinel-ingested Defender for Endpoint). Follows a *matching Microsoft 365 list item* across observed renames/moves where its identifier is populated; **does not prove descendant copies, track file contents, or verify current location**. Matching a historical path can return different file instances over time. The graph distinguishes observed movement edges from actor/activity edges.

content.query:
union isfuzzy=true
(OfficeActivity | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange} | summarize Records=count() | extend Table='OfficeActivity'),
(DeviceFileEvents | where TimeGenerated {TimeRange} | summarize Records=count() | extend Table='DeviceFileEvents')
| project Table, Records
content.title: Telemetry availability
File investigation overview

## 1. Movement and access relationship graph
**Blue/other location nodes** represent observed file paths; **identity nodes** represent accounts. Edges are either recorded file moves/copies or account activities. A graph edge does **not** imply the latest/current location without a fresh inventory check. The graph limits high-volume data to keep it readable.

content.title: Identity / file-location relationship graph

content.json:
## 2. Last observed locations
These are the latest appearances of each location in the searched logs, **not** an authoritative inventory of existing copies.

content.title: Last seen file paths

content.json:
## 3. Activity trend and detailed chronological timeline
Trend shows counts per day, including audit operations such as accesses and modifications. Grid below lists **events from oldest to newest** (up to 2,500 most recent matching records). Some access events may be throttled or omitted by the telemetry source.

content.title: File activity volume over time
Chronological file activity and evidence (UTC)

content.json:
## 4. Explicit movement and copy records
Only source-to-destination transitions **present in recorded telemetry** are included. Download does not establish an endpoint destination. A rename is not a new content copy.

content.title: Recorded moves and copies

content.json:
## 5. Accounts involved
An account in the log is the **recorded principal**, not conclusive human attribution. Entra sign-in enrichment is not joined in this v1 view.

---
### Interpretive guidance
- `PATH_MATCH`: event relates directly to the path/URL supplied. `SAME_M365_ITEM_ID`: the Microsoft 365 item identifier links an event to a directly matched event.
- **File path is not a globally stable ID.** Different files can occupy the same path at different times. Copies often get new IDs; hashes are supporting evidence, not provenance proof.
- **MDE does not guarantee a read/open event for every access**. Audit collection, permissions, licences, connectors and retention determine visibility.
- The evidence table retains event references for checking each transition in the source systems.
- **Operational improvement:** enrich this read-only workbook with Microsoft Graph `driveId/itemId`, version history, current item metadata, endpoint inventory, and Entra sign-in context via a separate evidence-correlation pipeline.

Source documentation: Microsoft Learn `OfficeActivity`, `DeviceFileEvents`, and Azure Workbook graph visualisations.
